_comment: request_user_input contract, generated from the codex binary itself:
codex app-server generate-json-schema --experimental --out <dir>
Same provenance as codex-method-contract.json / codex-turn-schema.json.
WHAT THIS FILE DOES: it pins the question shapes slice 3's bridge reads and
the answer body it writes, so a field the bridge invents (or one it drops)
is a red test rather than a -32602 on a machine we cannot reach.
WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it is a COMMITTED SNAPSHOT and cannot notice drift by
itself. A codex upgrade only shows up here if somebody re-runs the command
above. Treat 'bump codex -> regenerate this file' as part of the upgrade,
not as something the test suite will remind you about.
Every block carries `_from` = the generated file it was lifted out of.
`required` / `propertyNames` are verbatim; `propertyNames` is the key list
of that block's `properties`. Blocks whose name ends in `Type` quote a
single `type` node verbatim rather than a shape.
2026-08-26 UPGRADE 0.145.0 -> 0.149.1: this is the ONLY contract snapshot the
upgrade moved. ToolRequestUserInputParams gained isBlocking: boolean, and it is
REQUIRED, not optional -- five required keys now, six properties. Upstream also
marked autoResolutionMs @deprecated in the same release: "Use `isBlocking` to
decide whether the request should block." The bridge still only passes
autoResolutionMs through (readAutoResolutionMs), so nothing breaks today, but the
field it forwards is the deprecated half of that pair.
Everything else in the question family -- Question / Option / Response / Answer /
ServerRequestResolvedNotification -- re-generated byte-identical.
